finding: The bundled LibreCAD writer represents a full-circle MPOLYGON arc as two half-circle bulges. The upstream polyline-only policy initially refused that boundary.
change: Project a one-edge full circular arc to a closed two-vertex polyline with signed unit bulges, provided its angular span is within eight machine epsilons of one full turn and its endpoint offsets and diameter meet the radius-relative precision guard. Other arc profiles retain the previous path or are refused by the opt-in policy.
verification: Before the change, all eight exact-circle direction/encoding/policy profiles failed the expected projection; they pass afterwards.

The generated matrix covers seven DXF revisions, ASCII/Binary, both directions, default and polyline-only modes, full-circle output, near-full and large-coordinate fallback, invalid-radius failure followed by same-writer retry, original source state and boundary-handle readback.
ezdxf 1.4.5 reconstructs both semicircles' centers, radii, sweep and orientation for four independent ASCII/Binary and direction profiles; the optional peer tool creates and removes scratch files.
The upstream-linked LibreCAD DIMASSOC/MPOLYGON selector remains 12/12 passing, and adjacent HATCH/MPOLYGON tests pass.
limits: The angular-span tolerance normalizes deviations within eight machine epsilons of one turn; it is not an exact raw-angle preservation claim.
Only isolated one-edge circles are projected; mixed-edge full circles, native rendering, arbitrary applications and 3D consumer behavior remain unqualified.
No DWG or DXF fixture files were added.
